scope: First remote feedback remediation; public code and synthetic scenarios only.

history.note: All prior runs are preserved. Two question runs failed bounded wording checks despite correct endpoint/ascertainment advice. Two ML runs failed: one used an unsupported buffered-scaffold layout; the other hit an arbitrary Riley-to-assumption proximity limit. Both also had false AUPRC negation warnings. The prose graders were corrected, and the ML fixture now explicitly requests the documented module-import/direct-split layout. The final question pair is retained; new ML and omics pairs cover the final source/grammar changes. The same artifact/agreement condition was extended to the three unflagged equivalent advice cases, with new pairs for each. Original hashes/reports were not rewritten or rescored.

soft_review_notes.quoted_output: Do not label AUPRC the primary metric
soft_review_notes.reason: The label refusal is outside the bounded predicate vocabulary. The original 93/95 score is preserved; all hard gates and the frozen weighted threshold pass. No rescore or new vocabulary patch was used to force a perfect score.

jev.note: One complete unabridged initial code/test/eval patch input was supplied; service reported truncation and low confidence. Not retried. Later bounded grader corrections have separate source/evidence verification; this remains an unresolved advisory snapshot.

late_grader_verification.direct_check: The two contradicted source claims were rechecked against the exact current criteria and targeted executable controls: 2 tests and 20 assertions passed. No advisory was retried or represented as a passing full-patch gate.

limits: Two observations per case do not establish reliability or clinical validity.

The final shared-scorer delta changes claim_absent only. The retained question pair uses regex/JSON criteria and is unaffected; its recorded whole-scorer hash differs and is disclosed. ML and omics have fresh pairs under the final claim grammar.
Prose checks detect bounded phrases and canonical decision agreement, not arbitrary semantic contradictions.
Python provenance checking is bounded static analysis, not execution or a full language analysis.
BAM tests use synthetic samtools stubs; header evidence does not prove sequence identity.
Five optional tests require unrelated website, trial-engine, Parquet, workbook-rendering or Python numerical dependencies.
The ML fixture acceptance is restricted to module imports and explicit/cached split-pair loops; unsupported buffered layouts remain outside the static checker.
The bot docstring percentage was not independently reproduced. Four nontrivial missing helper contracts were documented; seven pre-existing lint findings remain outside scoped blocks.
